angle: Which strong long-term-memory systems can be reproduced on a weak laptop (i5, 16 GB RAM, 6 GB GPU) using only remote LLM APIs, with usable code and a permissive license. For each system I checked primary sources: arXiv papers, the official repos and their code, and released per-question artifacts. That includes files I streamed and parsed myself: the headers of the AMB outputs/*.json.gz files and the mem0 results/{platform,oss}/*.json files, a few MB each, with no datasets downloaded. Each number is labelled with what it measures, the denominator, the reader and judge models, and whether artifacts exist. No local models or benchmarks were run.

items.system: Hindsight (vectorize-io/hindsight) v0.4.19, in the vendor's own Agent Memory Benchmark (AMB) harness
items.variant: 'local' variant: embedded Hindsight with gemini-2.5-flash-lite as the retain/extraction LLM, rag mode, single recall with budget=high, max_tokens=32768 facts plus max_chunk_tokens=16384 of raw chunk text inlined
items.benchmark: LongMemEval-S cleaned (longmemeval_s_cleaned.json, Sept-2025 release), one memory bank per question
items.metric: End-to-end QA accuracy judged by an LLM (binary correct/incorrect)
items.denominator_exclusions: All 500 questions, including the 30 _abs questions. AMB has no dedicated abstention judge prompt: its longmemeval.py uses per-category prompts only. The SSU/SSA/MS prompt is a paraphrase of the official one, not the exact text.
items.reader: gemini-3.1-pro-preview. The answer prompt is LongMemEval-tuned: 'if you have 2 possible answers, just say both', comprehensive answers, and examples such as 'american football vs soccer, shows vs podcasts'
items.judge: gemini-2.5-flash-lite with AMB's category prompts (JSON correct=true/false)
items.budget: Average context of 43,624.5 tokens per question sent to the reader, about 38% of the ~115k-token haystack
items.cost_latency: From the artifact header: ingestion_time_ms 30,090,034 (about 8.4 h wall clock for the full run), avg_retrieve_time_ms 674.9, ingested_docs 11,303. My estimate: about 57M haystack tokens go through the extraction LLM in 3,000-char chunks, roughly 77k retain calls plus prompt overhead. That is roughly $12-30 with flash-lite at $0.10/$0.40 per M. The reader adds about 21.8M input tokens, about $44 at an assumed ~$2/M for gemini-3.1-pro.
items.code_license: MIT. The hindsight repo has 29.4k stars and was pushed 2026-09-25. The harness (vectorize-io/agent-memory-benchmark) has 83 stars, and its repo metadata shows no SPDX license.
items.artifacts: Yes. The per-question outputs with answer, reasoning and full retrieved context are at outputs/longmemeval/hindsight/rag/s.json.gz (28 MB) in the AMB repo.
items.notes: This is the strongest publicly verifiable artifact among the high scorers. Caveats: it is a vendor-built harness; it uses a non-official judge and a lenient, tuned answer prompt; and the reader gets 43.6k tokens of context. The current AMB adapter code sets enable_observations=False, while the March-2026 blog credits 'observations' for the gain, so it cannot be verified which setting produced this file. The run ingested 11,303 docs while AMB's hybrid-search run ingested 23,867; I could not explain the difference. Laptop-feasible defaults: embedded Postgres (pg0), local BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 embeddings and cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 reranker, all CPU-capable, with a remote LLM.

items.variant: Same as the LongMemEval run (locomo-hindsight run)
items.metric: End-to-end QA accuracy judged by an LLM
items.denominator_exclusions: The 446 category-5 adversarial questions are excluded (1,986 - 446 = 1,540)
items.budget: Average context of 36,235.4 tokens per question. That is more than a whole LoCoMo conversation: SmartSearch measures full context at 26,792 tokens, so this is effectively full-context reading.
items.cost_latency: Ingestion took 330 s (272 session docs). Retrieval averaged 964 ms. My estimate: reader input ≈ 1,540 × 36k ≈ 56M tokens, which dominates the cost (about $110 at ~$2/M).
items.notes: Because the context exceeds the conversation length, this result says little about retrieval quality. Compare the locomo-audit finding that full-context gpt-4.1-mini with a CoT prompt reaches 92.62%.

items.variant: OSS-20B: gpt-oss-20b for memory and answering. OSS-120B: gpt-oss-120b. Gemini-3: Gemini-3 Pro used only as the final answer generator.
items.benchmark: LongMemEval-S, 500 questions (original vs cleaned not stated)
items.metric: QA accuracy judged by an LLM
items.value: 91.4% (Gemini-3) / 89.0% (OSS-120B) / 83.6% (OSS-20B), versus 39.0% for a full-context OSS-20B baseline. Gemini-3 per category: SSU 97.1, SSA 96.4, SSP 80.0, KU 94.9, TR 91.0, MS 87.2.
items.judge: GPT-OSS-120B at temperature 0.0, not the official gpt-4o judge
items.budget: Not stated: the paper's token-budget cells contain '<add>' placeholders
items.cost_latency: Not quantified
items.artifacts: A 'Hindsight Benchmarks Viewer' (benchmarks.hindsight.vectorize.io) advertises downloadable results. The hindsight-benchmarks GitHub repo now holds a model-choice leaderboard, not LongMemEval per-question files.
items.notes: The README calls the result 'independently reproduced' by Virginia Tech and The Washington Post. Those groups appear to be co-author affiliations (Srivastava, Wang, Ramakrishnan and others are paper authors), so this is not an independent replication. Reranker: cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2.

items.variant: Gemini-3 / OSS-120B / OSS-20B
items.benchmark: LoCoMo (single-hop, multi-hop, open-domain, temporal; adversarial handling not described)
items.metric: QA accuracy judged by an LLM
items.value: 89.61% / 85.67% / 83.18%. The paper says this beats 75.78% for 'the strongest prior open system' (Memobase). Gemini-3 per category: single-hop 86.17, multi-hop 70.83, open-domain 95.12, temporal 83.80.
items.denominator_exclusions: Not explicitly stated. The paper's dataset description could not be reconciled with LoCoMo10.
items.cost_latency: Not stated
items.notes: Superseded by the AMB v0.4.19 numbers above

items.system: Hindsight (self-hosted) re-run by a competitor in MemTensor's OmniMemEval harness
items.variant: local/self-hosted Hindsight; memory-service LLM gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14
items.benchmark: LongMemEval-S cleaned, 500 questions / LoCoMo 1,540 questions (category 5 excluded)
items.metric: QA accuracy judged by an LLM
items.value: LongMemEval 72.20% (SSU 82.86, SSA 14.29, SSP 96.67, TR 82.71, MS 71.43, KU 78.21) with 29,755 context tokens. LoCoMo 81.99% (cloud) with 24,683 context tokens.
items.budget: Context tokens as listed in the value field
items.cost_latency: Not reported
items.artifacts: Only a results snapshot in docs/user_memory/results.md; per-question outputs not verified
items.notes: This is a competitor harness in which the vendor's own MemOS comes first. SSA at 14.29% points to an ingestion or adapter problem, such as assistant turns not being retained. Still, it shows a 22-point swing across harnesses for the same system.

items.variant: Qdrant with dense Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (1024-d, asymmetric) and sparse BM42 (bm42-all-minilm-l6-v2-attentions). Documents chunked into 512-token windows; RRF fusion; top-k 50 chunks (prefetch 100 per branch). No LLM at ingestion.
items.metric: End-to-end QA accuracy judged by an LLM
items.denominator_exclusions: All 500 questions, including abstention (no dedicated abstention prompt)
items.reader: gemini-3.1-pro-preview, with the same tuned AMB prompt as the Hindsight run
items.cost_latency: Ingestion 57,815,934 ms (about 16 h, dominated by local embedding of about 57M tokens); retrieval about 1.6 s; 23,867 docs ingested. On a 6 GB GPU the 0.6B embedder is fine; on CPU it would take many hours. The reader costs about $23 at ~$2/M (estimate).
items.code_license: The AMB repo shows no SPDX license (qdrant and fastembed themselves are Apache-2.0)
items.notes: This is the closest public, per-question-verified analogue of HybridMind's dense+sparse RRF path. Hindsight's lead over it in the same harness is 20.6 points on LongMemEval (94.6 vs 74.0).

items.variant: Same configuration as above
items.metric: QA accuracy judged by an LLM
items.budget: Average context of 22,156.5 tokens, close to full-conversation size
items.cost_latency: Ingestion 646 s; retrieval 219 ms
items.notes: Cognee in the same harness scored 80.26%, but only on 152 of the 1,540 questions (a partial run).

items.variant: Every turn is embedded as '[date] role: content' with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (local; 256-wordpiece truncation). Top-42 turns by cosine similarity. LLM call 1 is a CoT fact-extraction prompt over the 42 turns (max 512 output tokens). LLM call 2 answers from the facts, the raw turns and question_date (max 256 tokens). temperature 0.
items.benchmark: LongMemEval-S original (./data/longmemeval_s.json, not the cleaned release)
items.metric: QA accuracy judged by an LLM, using the official LongMemEval prompts copied verbatim, including the abstention prompt
items.judge: gpt-4o-2024-08-06 with the official category and abstention prompts
items.budget: 42 turns, about 10k tokens (my estimate), passed twice
items.cost_latency: Blog median latency 3.59 s per item. No LLM calls at ingestion: MiniLM embedding of roughly 500 turns per question works on CPU. My estimate: about 21k input + 0.7k output tokens per question, so roughly $30 for 500 questions with gpt-4o, or about $5 with a mini-class reader.
items.code_license: No license file (GitHub license: null), which means all rights reserved. Reimplement the roughly 40-line mechanism rather than copying it. 13 stars; last push 2026-04-21.
items.artifacts: No per-question outputs released. main.py prints aggregate and per-type accuracy only.
items.notes: This has the clearest mechanism and the cheapest faithful reproduction on a weak laptop. It stores nothing beyond embeddings. The result is self-reported and has no released artifacts.

items.variant: Simple: match on turns, retrieve whole sessions, and score each session by the NDCG of its turns after cross-encoder reranking, followed by a simple CoT answer. Internal: undisclosed.
items.metric: QA accuracy judged by an LLM (official evaluation)
items.value: Simple 82.4% (7.12 s per item); Simple Faster 76.8% (top-20, 2.97 s); Internal 86.0% (5.65 s). Baselines from the same post: Naive RAG 52.0%; full-context GPT-4o 63.8% (Emergence's run) vs 60.2% (Zep's run); full-context o3 76.0%; Accumulator (a Chain-of-Note variant) 81.8% at 111.8 s; Oracle GPT-4o 82.4%.
items.budget: Top-42 turns (Simple) / 20 turns (Simple Faster); number of sessions in context not stated
items.cost_latency: Median latencies as listed in the value field
items.notes: Mastra and others point out that the 86% 'Internal' result cannot be reproduced. The 'Simple' mechanism (turn hits leading to session expansion scored by NDCG) is fully described and easy to reimplement on top of HybridMind's retrieval.

items.variant: Observer and Reflector run as background agents (the research run used gemini-2.5-flash). Observation triggers at 30k message tokens, reflection at 40k observation tokens, with async buffering at 20% and 5k-token observer batches in the benchmark config. The reader sees a stable, append-only observation log of about 30k tokens. No vector DB or retrieval by default.
items.benchmark: LongMemEval-S, 500 questions. The data-download guide points to the original xiaowu0162/longmemeval, not the cleaned release.
items.metric: QA accuracy judged by an LLM
items.value: gpt-5-mini reader 94.87% (KU 96.2, MS 87.2, SSA 94.6, SSP 100.0, SSU 95.7, TR 95.5). gemini-3-pro 93.27%. gemini-3-flash 89.20%. gpt-4o reader 84.23% (compared with 82.40% for oracle gpt-4o as cited).
items.denominator_exclusions: 500 questions; the evaluator has an official abstention branch
items.reader: As listed in the value field
items.judge: openai/gpt-4o with the official LongMemEval prompts copied verbatim into longmemeval-metric.ts
items.budget: About 30k tokens of context on average
items.cost_latency: My estimate: the observer reads about 57M haystack tokens in roughly 11.5k calls of 5k-token batches, and the observer prompt is about 873 lines. That is roughly $80-120 with gemini-2.5-flash ($0.30/$2.50 per M). The reader adds 500 × 30k ≈ 15M tokens, about $7 with gpt-5-mini.
items.code_license: Apache-2.0 core, but ee/ directories are under the Mastra Enterprise License. 28.3k stars. TypeScript/Node. Storage is LibSQL (a local file) or Postgres.
items.artifacts: No per-question outputs: explorations/longmemeval/.gitignore excludes /results. The benchmark runner code is public.
items.notes: There is a contamination risk. The repo's INVESTIGATION_WORKFLOW.md iterates on failed test questions, applies 'fixes' (Observer/Reflector prompt changes, 'improved Q/A') and syncs them into longmemeval_s.json. config.ts contains dozens of OM variants, and which one produced 94.87% is not pinned. Mechanism clarity is high.

items.system: Mem0 Platform (managed, v3 algorithm), as stated in the README
items.variant: Top-200 retrieved memories; single-pass ADD-only extraction; semantic, BM25 and entity-boost fusion
items.metric: QA accuracy judged by an LLM (PASS/FAIL)
items.value: README: 94.4% (472/500) at top-200 and 94.8% at top-50. The committed artifact results/platform/longmemeval_results.json says 93.4% (467/500), and longmemeval_top50_results.json says 90.4% (452/500).
items.judge: gpt-5 with mem0's own JUDGE_PROMPT, which is more lenient than the official one: 'rough answers are correct', '8 months and 20 days matches 9 months', generous date windows
items.budget: About 6.9k tokens per query (mem0 claim) for 200 memories
items.cost_latency: Managed service; not reproducible locally
items.code_license: The harness is Apache-2.0 (116 stars); the platform itself is closed
items.artifacts: Yes: results/platform/*.json. They do not match the README headline numbers.
items.notes: The answer prompt contains LongMemEval-specific examples (for instance a 'Sales Manager vs Senior Sales Engineer' abstention case). I parsed the committed files directly to find the README/artifact mismatch.

items.variant: Top-200 / top-50
items.metric: QA accuracy judged by an LLM
items.value: README: 92.5% (1425/1540), 91.8% at top-50. Committed artifact: 91.56% (1410/1540) at top-200 (single-hop 92.3, multi-hop 93.3, temporal 92.8, open-domain 76.0), and 82.66% at top-50.
items.denominator_exclusions: Categories [1,2,3,4], 1,540 questions. metadata.merged_from_questions lists 156 IDs (top-200) and 274 IDs (top-50) merged in from re-runs.
items.judge: gpt-5 with mem0's LoCoMo judge. Issue #30 reports 88.46% under the original Zep/Mem0 judge versus 94.32% with the current one on the same answers.
items.cost_latency: n/a
items.notes: GitHub issue #30 raises answer-prompt hints that match gold answers, the merged re-runs, and the judge change. No maintainer reply was visible.

items.variant: Mem0 server (FastAPI) with Qdrant via docker-compose. One add() per user+assistant pair (CHUNK_SIZE=2), each triggering an extraction LLM call. The reported runs used a Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B embedder via SageMaker, not the default text-embedding-3-small. Top-200.
items.metric: QA accuracy judged by an LLM (mem0 judge)
items.value: 91.0% with GPT-5 as extraction LLM (SSU 95.7, SSA 92.9, SSP 93.3, KU 91.0, TR 94.7, MS 83.5). 89.8% with GPT-OSS-120B, 88.6% with Llama-4-Maverick, 88.6% with Gemma-4-31B.
items.judge: gpt-5, with the lenient custom prompt
items.cost_latency: My estimate: about 250 pairs per question gives about 125k extraction calls for the full run. At about 2-4k tokens per call that is 250-500M input tokens: roughly $40-75 with the default gpt-4o-mini, or several hundred dollars with GPT-5. The query stage is small (500 × about 7k tokens).
items.code_license: mem0 is Apache-2.0 (66.0k stars; pushed 2026-09-25); the harness is Apache-2.0
items.notes: On a laptop, Docker plus Qdrant is light, and LLM and embeddings can be remote. Independent numbers for Mem0 vary widely: 56.00% (OmniMemEval, cloud, gpt-4.1-mini) and 67.56% (TiMem, GPT-4o), while a DEV.to independent run reports 32.4% for OSS (secondary).

items.variant: 'raw' mode: ChromaDB with the default all-MiniLM-L6-v2. One document per session made of user turns only. No LLM.
items.metric: Session-level recall_any@5: is any gold session among the top 5 of about 50 sessions. This is not QA accuracy.
items.value: 96.6% (per type: KU 99.0, MS 98.5, TR 96.2, SSU 95.7, SSP 93.3, SSA 92.9). Hybrid v4 (keyword, temporal and name boosts, no LLM) scores 98.4% R@5 and 99.8% R@10 on a 450-question held-out split tuned on 50 dev questions. A 100% result with Haiku/Sonnet rerank was admitted to be tuned on test failures.
items.denominator_exclusions: 500 questions, including the 30 abstention ones. The official LongMemEval retrieval evaluation skips those 30, giving 470.
items.cost_latency: Zero API calls; CPU only
items.artifacts: Yes: benchmarks/results_raw_full500.jsonl and others, per the repo
items.notes: No end-to-end QA accuracy is published. Useful only as a retrieval-stage reference. The critical-analysis paper arXiv 2604.21284 documents the teaching-to-the-test history. rohitg00/agentmemory reports on the same metric: BM25-only 86.2%, BM25+vector 95.2%.

items.variant: Hybrid v5 at session granularity, top-10, no rerank
items.benchmark: LoCoMo10, all 1,986 QA pairs, including adversarial
items.metric: Session recall@10 / recall@5
items.value: R@10 88.9%, R@5 83.7%. Session baseline R@10 60.3%. A 100% result with Sonnet at top-50 is structurally invalid because top-50 exceeds the 19-32 sessions in each conversation.
items.cost_latency: CPU only
items.notes: Retrieval only; not comparable to QA accuracy

items.variant: Retrievers: flat-bm25, flat-contriever, flat-stella (Stella V5 1.5B) and flat-gte (gte-Qwen2-7B), at turn or session granularity. Optional key expansion (session-summ/keyphrase/userfact, turn-keyphrase/userfact) with separate, merge or replace join modes. Optional time-aware query pruning. Reader uses the con (Chain-of-Note) method with the JSON history format; default topk_context is 50.
items.benchmark: Paper retrieval and RAG experiments on LongMemEval_M (~500 sessions); full-context on S
items.metric: QA accuracy (gpt-4o judge, over 97% agreement with humans); retrieval Recall@k and NDCG@k
items.value: Full-context GPT-4o on S: 60.6% (no CoN). Oracle GPT-4o: 87.0% (no CoN) and 92.4% (CoN plus JSON). Best RAG with GPT-4o on M: about 65.7-71.4% (session values, key = value + userfact). Stella session retrieval with K=V+fact: Recall@5 0.732, NDCG@5 0.620. Time-aware query expansion adds about 11.3% (rounds) and 6.8% (sessions) recall on temporal questions.
items.denominator_exclusions: QA uses 500 questions. Retrieval metrics always skip the 30 abstention instances (470).
items.judge: gpt-4o-2024-08-06 via evaluate_qa.py (official category and abstention prompts)
items.budget: Top-k configurable; the RAG default is 50
items.cost_latency: BM25 runs on CPU with zero cost. Stella 1.5B fits a 6 GB GPU in fp16; gte-7B does not. The reader supports OpenAI directly, or any OpenAI-compatible base URL (vLLM), so remote APIs work. Key expansion needs one LLM call per session unless you reuse the released caches, which were built on the pre-cleaning data.
items.artifacts: Released key-expansion and timestamped-event caches; no per-question RAG hypothesis files
items.notes: This is the reference protocol HybridMind should match: official evaluate_qa.py, 500 questions including abstention, and recall_any/recall_all at session and turn level. Numbers were extracted from the arXiv HTML; the M-vs-S split of the RAG table should be re-checked against Table 3 of arXiv 2410.10813.

items.variant: Zep service. Episodes are ingested with separate LLM steps for entity extraction and resolution, fact extraction and resolution, temporal extraction, and edge invalidation, as described in the paper.
items.metric: QA accuracy judged by an LLM
items.value: 71.2% (gpt-4o) vs 60.2% full-context; 63.8% (gpt-4o-mini) vs 55.4% full-context. Single-session-assistant drops 9-17.7%.
items.judge: GPT-4o with the LongMemEval question-specific prompts
items.cost_latency: About 90% latency reduction (for example 3.20 s vs 31.3 s)
items.code_license: Graphiti is Apache-2.0 (31.2k stars). It needs Neo4j, FalkorDB, or embedded Kuzu. The Zep service is closed.
items.artifacts: The paper promises notebooks; getzep/zep-papers has a LoCoMo eval script
items.notes: Zep's 2026 site claims 94.7% LoCoMo and 90.2% LongMemEval with 5,760 / 4,408 context tokens. A third-party audit says these used GPT-5.4 with an unpublished judge prompt, so I could not verify them. OmniMemEval ran graphiti-zep self-hosted and got 79.80% on LongMemEval-S cleaned, but with 117,106 context tokens (more than the haystack), which suggests an adapter artifact.

items.variant: Zep re-run by Zep vs by Mem0
items.metric: QA accuracy judged by an LLM
items.value: The original 84% claim included category 5 inconsistently. Mem0's re-run gave 58.44% ± 0.20 over 10 runs; Zep's corrected re-run gave 75.14% ± 0.17.
items.cost_latency: Zep reports p95 search latency of 0.632 s
items.artifacts: Zep artifacts are linked from memobase issue #101
items.notes: This dispute shows how much the adapter and prompt choices move LoCoMo scores

items.variant: MemCell/MemScene construction with hybrid dense+BM25 RRF plus rerank. Old stack: MongoDB, Elasticsearch, Milvus and Redis via Docker. New EverOS: Markdown, SQLite and LanceDB, local-first.
items.metric: QA accuracy judged by an LLM
items.value: Paper: LoCoMo 93.05% (gpt-4.1-mini) and 86.76% (gpt-4o-mini); LongMemEval 83.00%, with LongMemEval baselines taken from the MemOS leaderboard rather than re-run. Evaluation README (v1.0.0): LoCoMo 92.32% vs full-context 91.21%, both gpt-4.1-mini.
items.reader: gpt-4.1-mini with a multi-step CoT answer prompt
items.judge: gpt-4o-mini plus two auxiliary judges, averaged (per the paper)
items.cost_latency: Multiple LLM calls at ingestion for boundary detection and episode/profile extraction
items.artifacts: Evaluation framework released; per-question outputs not verified
items.notes: Reproducibility is disputed. EverOS issue #73 reports 38.38% on LoCoMo with the full Docker stack, and the issue was closed without an answer. locomo-audit finds full-context gpt-4.1-mini with the same CoT prompt scores 92.62%, which exceeds EverMemOS. The old stack is too heavy for a 16 GB laptop. OmniMemEval re-run: EverOS 80.40% on LongMemEval and 82.75% on LoCoMo.

items.variant: Full conversation in context, answer_prompt_cot
items.benchmark: LoCoMo10, 1,540 questions (category 5 not scored: 446 adversarial questions, broken implementation)
items.metric: QA accuracy judged by an LLM, plus an answer-key audit
items.value: Full-context gpt-4.1-mini with CoT: 92.62%. 99 of 1,540 gold answers (6.4%) are wrong, which caps the score at 93.57%. The gpt-4o-mini judge accepts 62.81% of deliberately wrong but topical answers.
items.cost_latency: n/a
items.code_license: CC BY-NC 4.0, matching the LoCoMo dataset license
items.notes: This means LoCoMo scores near 92% carry no memory-system signal unless context is at least 5× smaller than the conversation

items.system: MemOS (MemTensor), in its own OmniMemEval harness
items.variant: MemOS cloud
items.metric: QA accuracy judged by an LLM
items.value: LongMemEval 89.20% (SSU 100, SSA 100, SSP 100, TR 89.47, MS 78.95, KU 84.62) with 4,151 context tokens. LoCoMo 88.83% with 5,400 context tokens.
items.cost_latency: n/a
items.code_license: MemOS is Apache-2.0 (11.6k stars). Self-hosting needs Neo4j and Qdrant.
items.artifacts: Results snapshot only (not verified per question)
items.notes: The vendor runs the harness and its own product ranks first. The result is from the cloud service, not the OSS code. Neo4j is heavy on a 16 GB laptop.

items.variant: Sensory pre-compression with LLMLingua-2, topic-segmented short-term memory, and an offline 'sleep-time' long-term update; all-MiniLM-L6-v2 retrieval
items.metric: QA accuracy judged by an LLM
items.value: LongMemEval-S: 68.64% (GPT-4o-mini) and 73.20% (Qwen3-30B-A3B), versus NaiveRAG 61.00% and FullText 56.80% (GPT-4o-mini). LoCoMo: 72.99% (GPT-4o-mini) versus FullText 71.83%.
items.denominator_exclusions: 500 questions. Five corrupted samples (indices 74, 183, 278, 351, 380) were skipped by LightMem and counted as incorrect.
items.budget: Small (about 0.7k answer tokens per question in the reproduction)
items.cost_latency: The paper claims up to 38× fewer total tokens and 30× fewer API calls. The reproduction measured 72.7k-119.9k construction tokens and 65-118 construction LLM calls per sample.
items.notes: The LLMLingua-2 compressor (XLM-R-large) runs on a 6 GB GPU

items.system: Reproducing LightMem (ielab): naive RAG vs LightMem
items.variant: Naive RAG over raw user turns only, with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (11 retrievers tested), top-k 3, 5 or 10
items.metric: QA accuracy judged by an LLM
items.value: At top-10: naive RAG 67.3%, LightMem 68.2% (r=0.6) and 70.7% (r=0.8). Swapping only the retriever moves LightMem from 58.1% (BM25) to 75.5% (Qwen3-Emb-4B). On gold turns, naive RAG reaches 89.0% vs 77.7% for LightMem.
items.denominator_exclusions: The 56 single-session-assistant questions are excluded because LightMem ingests only user turns (500 − 56 = 444)
items.budget: About 1.03k answer tokens per question for naive RAG vs 18.84k for full context
items.cost_latency: LightMem needs about 321 questions to amortise its construction cost
items.code_license: Paper under the arXiv license; code at ielab/Reproducing-LightMem (1 star, no license)
items.notes: Independent evidence that an extraction layer adds little over verbatim-turn RAG once the retriever is fixed

items.variant: Index-free: spaCy NER-weighted substring matching (grep) over raw history, rule-based entity expansion for multi-hop, then mxbai-rerank-large-v1 cross-encoder (435M) plus ColBERT fused with RRF (k=60, wCE=0.7, wCB=0.3). No LLM at ingestion or retrieval.
items.metric: QA accuracy judged by an LLM
items.value: LongMemEval-S: 88.4% index-free and 87.6% indexed (KU 92.3, MS 79.7, SSA 87.5, SSP 96.7, SSU 95.7, TR 86.5). LoCoMo: 93.5% (EverMemOS protocol) / 91.9% (MemOS protocol). Oracle passage recall 98.6%, but only 22.5% of gold evidence survives truncation to the budget without ranking.
items.denominator_exclusions: The paper says '500 questions ... excluding abstention', which is internally ambiguous (470 or 500)
items.judge: EverMemOS protocol (gpt-4.1-mini answer and judge, multi-step CoT) or MemOS protocol (gpt-4o-mini)
items.budget: 2,000 words, about 3,141 tokens on LoCoMo (full context there is 26,792)
items.cost_latency: About 650 ms per query on CPU
items.code_license: Paper CC BY 4.0; no public code (commercial Midbrain product)
items.notes: The mechanism is clear and CPU-only, a strong design reference for HybridMind's sparse path. It cannot be reproduced without reimplementation, and the CoT answer protocol inflates LoCoMo scores.

items.system: ReFind (agent-controlled BM25 search over raw chat logs)
items.variant: BM25 at turn granularity (k1=1.2, b=0.75) with RRF of turn- and session-level scores. Each hit is expanded by ±2 neighbouring turns, with temporal narrowing and skipping of already-inspected sessions. About 2.5 searches and 4.99 LLM calls per question.
items.benchmark: LongMemEval-S subset (50 questions from STITCH) / M subset (15 questions)
items.metric: QA accuracy judged by an LLM, mean ± std over 5 runs
items.judge: gpt-4.1-mini with an explicitly generous rubric
items.cost_latency: 41-119 s per task
items.code_license: Paper CC BY 4.0; no code URL
items.notes: Low weight because of the 50-question subset and generous judge. The mechanism (BM25 plus neighbour expansion plus an agent loop) is directly relevant.

items.variant: Bi-temporal facts with hybrid semantic, keyword, graph and recency retrieval. LanceDB, Kuzu and SQLite, optionally Postgres; BGE embeddings. One LLM call per closed session, with optional per-turn fact extraction.

key_takeaways: Top 4 ranked by verified strength × feasibility × mechanism clarity. (1) Hindsight (MIT, 29.4k stars). It has the only high score backed by public per-question artifacts: 94.6% (473/500) on LongMemEval-S cleaned and 92.0% (1417/1540) on LoCoMo in the AMB repo. It runs on a laptop with embedded Postgres (pg0), bge-small embeddings and a MiniLM cross-encoder on CPU, with remote LLMs. It is marked down for a vendor harness with a lenient LongMemEval-tuned answer prompt, a gemini-2.5-flash-lite judge, 36-44k context tokens, 72.2% in MemTensor's harness, and about 8.4 h and tens of thousands of LLM calls to ingest LongMemEval-S. (2) EmergenceMem Simple Fast: 79.0% with gpt-4o and the official judge prompts. It uses MiniLM top-42 turns and two LLM calls, needs no ingestion LLM, and costs about $30 per full LongMemEval-S run. The mechanism is the clearest of all, but there are no artifacts and no license file, so reimplement it rather than copy it. The described 'Simple' variant reached 82.4% by scoring sessions on the NDCG of their cross-encoder-reranked turns. (3) Mem0 OSS through the memory-benchmarks harness (Apache-2.0, Docker + Qdrant), with committed per-question OSS files at 88.6-91.0%. The caveats: GPT-5 reader and judge, a custom lenient judge, a LongMemEval-specific answer prompt, costly per-pair extraction, and platform README numbers (94.4/92.5) that do not match the committed files (93.4/91.56, with 156 merged re-run questions). (4) Mastra OM: 94.87% with gpt-5-mini and 84.23% with a gpt-4o reader, judged by gpt-4o with the official prompts. It is Apache-2.0 core (TypeScript, LibSQL) and has no retrieval. However, no per-question outputs are released, and the repo's investigation workflow tunes prompts on failed test questions and edits dataset Q/A.

Harness choice moves scores by 20+ points, which is the dominant confound. Hindsight scores 94.6% in its own AMB harness and 72.2% in MemTensor's OmniMemEval. Mem0 ranges from 93.4-94.4% (own harness, GPT-5 judge) down to 56.0% (OmniMemEval). Zep's LoCoMo result has been reported as 84, 58.44 and 75.14. Mem0's custom judge gives 94.32% versus 88.46% for the original judge on the same answers. Treat any number without a pinned judge prompt, reader and per-question file as unverified. For HybridMind, report against the official evaluate_qa.py with the gpt-4o-2024-08-06 judge on all 500 questions including abstention, and state reader, top-k and context tokens.

LoCoMo is nearly saturated by full context. Full-context gpt-4.1-mini with a CoT prompt scores 92.62%. 6.4% of gold answers are wrong, capping the score at 93.57%, and the judge accepts 62.81% of wrong but topical answers. AMB's Hindsight and hybrid-search runs fed the reader 36k and 22k tokens, at or above LoCoMo conversation size. LoCoMo gains therefore mean nothing unless context is much smaller than the conversation. Prioritise LongMemEval-S and possibly M, where the ~115k-token haystack forces real retrieval.

Simple verbatim-retrieval baselines hold up well against extraction-heavy systems. AMB's dense+sparse RRF hybrid-search (Qwen3-Emb-0.6B + BM42, 512-token chunks, top-50) scores 74.0% on LongMemEval-S with gemini-3.1-pro, with per-question outputs public. Emergence Simple Fast reaches 79.0%. The independent LightMem reproduction finds naive user-turn RAG matches LightMem (67.3% vs 68.2-70.7%), and swapping only the retriever moves LightMem between 58.1% and 75.5%. SmartSearch (CPU grep, NER, cross-encoder and ColBERT, no LLM, closed code) claims 88.4% with gpt-4.1-mini. ReFind (BM25 turns with ±2-turn neighbour expansion and an agent loop) claims 93.2% on a 50-question subset. The lesson for HybridMind: retrieve at turn level, expand to neighbours or the whole session, rerank, and use a CoT reader.

For extraction-based systems, ingestion dominates cost. A full LongMemEval-S run pushes about 57M haystack tokens through the memory layer, because each of the 500 questions has its own ~115k-token haystack. These call counts are my estimates, not measured: Hindsight about 77k retain calls (3,000-char chunks); Mem0 OSS about 125k add() calls (one per user+assistant pair); Mastra OM about 11.5k observer calls (5k-token batches with an ~873-line prompt). Retrieval-only baselines need zero ingestion LLM calls. Remote embedding of the haystack is cheap (about 57M tokens), and deduplicating shared sessions may cut it further (unverified). LoCoMo ingestion is trivial (10 conversations), so its cost is all in the reader and scales with context size.

Retrieval-only numbers are a different quantity from QA accuracy. MemPalace's 96.6% R@5 is session-level recall_any@5 over ~50 sessions, with each session represented by user turns only, on all 500 questions including abstention. Its 98.4% held-out figure came after dev tuning, and its 100% after test tuning. agentmemory reports 95.2% for BM25+vector and 86.2% for BM25 alone; raya-ac/engram claims 98.1%. The official LongMemEval retrieval metric excludes the 30 abstention questions (470). None of these projects publish end-to-end QA accuracy. Use them only as retrieval-stage references and report recall_all and turn-level recall alongside.

Feasibility on an i5 with 16 GB RAM and a 6 GB GPU. Fine: Emergence-style in-memory retrieval (MiniLM on CPU), MemPalace (Chroma on CPU), Hindsight (embedded pg0 with CPU bge-small and MiniLM cross-encoder; remote LLM), Mastra OM (Node + LibSQL), Mem0 OSS (Docker Qdrant), and the official LongMemEval scripts (BM25 on CPU, Stella 1.5B in fp16 on the 6 GB GPU, remote reader through an OpenAI-compatible URL). Avoid: gte-Qwen2-7B locally, the old EverMemOS stack (MongoDB + Elasticsearch + Milvus + Redis), MemOS self-host (Neo4j + Qdrant), and Graphiti with Neo4j (embedded Kuzu is the lighter option).

Licences: MIT for Hindsight, MemPalace, LightMem, A-Mem, SeCom and LongMemEval (code and data). Apache-2.0 for mem0, memory-benchmarks, Graphiti, MemOS, EverOS and Memobase. Mastra is Apache-2.0 except ee/ directories. Engram (ly-wang19) is AGPL-3.0. emergence_simple_fast and ielab/Reproducing-LightMem have no licence file, and AMB's repo metadata shows no SPDX licence. The LoCoMo data is CC BY-NC 4.0. SmartSearch, ReFind, Agent Zero Memory (claims 95.6%) and Emergence's 86% 'Internal' variant have no public code, so they cannot be reproduced as-is.
